texts.label: A
fehler: "the chapel window held her reflection over his: her white shoes, his dark coat, the three stirrers lined up on the table between them" – the reflection in the door window is optically implausible from the corridor; the final image feels constructed
"She went in because the lights were on." – flat causal statement that explains rather than shows
"She touched it, though she couldn’t see the name." – the logic of the gesture is unclear
"Someone had arranged them parallel." – the symbolic detail is set up too deliberately
"His voice was ordinary, almost apologetic." – tells the reader instead of showing

texts.label: B
fehler: "**Second Pew**" – a title, which goes beyond the requested bare book text
"You sat with my mother. Room twelve. You did her hair." – explains the stranger, so it effectively ends on a revelation despite the closing image
"a single grey hair wound through its teeth like thread on a spool" – the comb with the mother's hair tips into sentimentality and feels contrived
"I just wanted to see what you looked like when you weren't busy." – an overly neat, epigrammatic line
"the only room on the fourth floor where the lights dimmed on their own" – the premise is vague and not quite logical

texts.label: C
fehler: "leaving a little white paper on the skin" – idiomatically weak; something like "a scrap of white paper" would be expected
"His coat was buttoned incorrectly" – stiff word choice ("buttoned wrong")
"She knew the gesture from relatives who had been asked too many questions by too many people." – a slightly explanatory interpretation
"He looked at the space beside him, then back at her." – this non-answer to the name question leaves the core premise somewhat underexploited

texts.label: D
fehler: "which was the first wrong thing" – a formulaic opening with no second "wrong thing" following
"The tealight shivered in its plastic cup, though no air moved." – brushes against a ghost-story cliché
"In eleven years she had learned that people at this hour usually supplied it unprompted" – narratorial explanation
"the way she wore it after a patient's daughter had once looked her up online" – backstory squeezed into a subordinate clause, which slows the scene

texts.label: E
fehler: "She didn't know a Miller on her floor. Miller worked pediatric oncology, two buildings over, and had retired in November." – a logical break: she claims not to know him, then knows his details
"made no sound on the linoleum, only a faint tackiness" – tackiness is not a sound, so the comparison misfires
"the font was twelve-point, illegible from twenty feet away" – over-explanation and implausibly precise
"Nora’s hand went instinctively to her chest" – a stock gesture plus a telling adverb
"a single melted gray slush-print was slowly soaking into the tight industrial weave" – adjective pile-up; the whole text is overwritten and over length
